title: Why Credo Technology Sank This Week
author: Billy Duberstein
description: Credo Technology stock plunged 29.5% this week despite beating earnings expectations with 114.7% revenue growth and 130% EPS growth. The sell-off was driven by margin pressure, with GAAP gross margins falling to 64.5% from 68% last quarter, and higher-than-expected stock-based compensation. At a valuation of ~50x true forward earnings when accounting for stock dilution, investors viewed the results as insufficient given the company's already high valuation.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock fell 29.5% despite beating revenue and earnings expectations. Margin compression (GAAP gross margins down to 64.5% from 68%), rising stock-based compensation, and deteriorating margin guidance spooked investors. While the company maintains strong triple-digit growth, the high valuation (~50x true forward earnings) left no room for disappointment.
Mentioned as a comparison point for Credo's AI infrastructure positioning. No direct news or sentiment impact discussed in the article.

title: 3 Millionaire-Maker Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks to Buy Now
author: Micah Zimmerman
description: The article highlights three AI infrastructure stocks—Astera Labs, Credo Technology, and Vertiv—that address critical bottlenecks in AI data center scaling. Astera Labs specializes in connectivity solutions with 93% YoY revenue growth and a $6.5B Amazon warrant agreement. Credo Technology manufactures active electrical cables with 272% YoY growth but faces customer concentration risks. Vertiv dominates power and cooling systems with a $15B backlog and strong positioning in liquid cooling demand.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong 93% YoY revenue growth, high 76.3% gross margins indicating design-focused business model, Scorpio product family expected to become largest product line, and strategic $6.5B warrant agreement with Amazon provide significant growth catalysts and validation.

Exceptional 272% YoY revenue growth with guidance above 200% for full-year, steep adoption curve for active electrical cables, and expanding product portfolio (ZeroFlap Optics, OmniConnect gearboxes). However, sentiment is tempered by significant customer concentration risk and high stock volatility.

Massive $15B backlog with 2.9 book-to-bill ratio indicating strong demand, binding purchase orders with advance payments, and strategic positioning in liquid cooling where lead times have extended significantly. Expanding manufacturing capacity by 40-50% demonstrates confidence in sustained demand.

Mentioned as a strategic partner through Astera Labs' $6.5B warrant agreement, indicating Amazon's commitment to AI infrastructure scaling, but no direct investment recommendation or analysis provided.

title: Why Credo Technology Stock Plunged 20% Today
author: Anders Bylund
description: Credo Technology's stock dropped 20% despite beating Q1 2027 earnings estimates with 115% revenue growth and 131% earnings growth. The decline was driven by concerns over high customer concentration (three clients account for 74% of revenue), elevated valuation multiples (59x trailing earnings), and high volatility (beta of 3.2), despite strong guidance for Q2.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While the company delivered exceptional financial results (115% revenue growth, 131% earnings growth) and raised guidance, the stock fell 20% due to investor concerns about extreme customer concentration (74% of revenue from three clients), already-high valuation multiples (59x trailing earnings), and the risk of demand cliff if major customers reduce orders. The market's reaction suggests these structural risks outweigh the strong operational performance.

title: Credo's Optical Bet: Is a $600M+ Revenue Opportunity Taking Shape?
author: Na
description: Credo Technology reported $479 million in Q1 FY2027 revenue, up 114.7% year-over-year, driven by strong demand for optical connectivity solutions in AI infrastructure. The company expects optical revenue to exceed $600 million in FY2027 with three product lines each contributing over $100 million. Competitors Marvell Technology and Astera Labs are also benefiting from the shift toward higher-speed connectivity and near-package optics in AI networks.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong revenue growth of 114.7% YoY with record optical DSP revenue and successful silicon photonics PIC integration. Expected inflection in H2 FY2027 with optical revenue exceeding $600 million and over 85% full-year growth. However, trading at premium valuation (14.24x forward P/S vs. industry 4.96x) and rated Hold.

Strong demand across optical DSPs, broadband analog, and switching businesses with 1.6T ramping rapidly. Multiple business segments tracking toward $1 billion annualized revenue run rates, with significant scale-up opportunity ahead.

Benefiting from rising demand for high-speed connectivity in AI infrastructure with diverse product portfolio (Taurus, CXL, UALink, optical). Expected Q3 revenue of $540-$560 million implies ~40% sequential growth with strong product shipments.

title: Marvell Technology (MRVL) Q2 Earnings and Revenues Beat Estimates
author: Na
description: Marvell Technology reported Q3 2026 earnings of $0.94 per share, beating consensus estimates of $0.93, with revenues of $2.74 billion exceeding expectations by 1.03%. The stock has gained 188.4% year-to-date and holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating. Meanwhile, Credo Technology Group is expected to report quarterly earnings of $1.16 per share (up 123.1% YoY) with revenues of $470.73 million when it reports on September 1.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Beat consensus EPS estimates by $0.01 (1.08% surprise), exceeded revenue expectations by 1.03%, demonstrated strong year-to-date performance (+188.4%), and received a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating with favorable estimate revision trends.
Expected to report exceptional earnings growth of 123.1% year-over-year with revenues up 111% from the prior year quarter, indicating strong business momentum in the semiconductor industry.
